title: EMOSA fleet configuration
description: The front port every pod is handed to, and the settings every agent it creates inherits.

advertise.description: Host the pods reach agent ports on; manager_addr becomes tcp:ADVERTISE:PORT.

forward.description: The package's forwarder (emosa-forward-c) exposes the front port and the agent ports, which listen on loopback, on the advertise address (an IPv4 address, a gateway's LAN address) where the pods reach them. Default false: another forwarder does (in the labs, an LXD proxy).

uplink.description: Given to every agent. Data plane option 1: the agent switches the pod's backhaul station onto the EasyMesh backhaul (data-plane.md §5.3, spec §8). Mode ethernet: a wired pod's uplink port bridged into br-home (spec §8.4). Absent or mode off: the pod keeps its OpenSync uplink (option 2).

mode.description: multi-ap: option 1 (spec §8.3); ethernet: a wired pod, its Ethernet uplink bridged into the fronthaul's bridge (spec §8.4).

port.description: With mode ethernet: the pod's Ethernet uplink port.

credentials.description: m2: the backhaul BSS of the controller's applied M2 set (multi_bss); config: ssid and secret_ref below.

secret_ref.description: A file in the agent's secret directory (state_dir/secrets), mode 0600.

bssid.description: The upstream backhaul BSS the station is pinned to, required with mode multi-ap. Never one of the pod's own BSSIDs: a station on its own backhaul BSS loops br-home.

hold_backoff.description: Seconds a failed switch holds the pod on option 2 before the switch is made again (spec §8.3), doubled with each held retry.

hold_backoff_cap.description: The longest hold between two retries, in seconds.

telemetry.description: Given to every agent (each subscribes to its own pod's topic). The pod's own statistics (spec §3.6): the agent sets the pod's MQTT settings and a raw client report once per OpenSync start, and subscribes to the pod's topic. Absent or mode off: the agent leaves the pod's statistics publishing alone.

broker.description: Broker host the pod connects to (mutual TLS with its device certificate).

subscribe.description: host:port where the agent reads the pod's topic.

publish_interval.description: qm's publish interval in seconds (mqtt_settings agg_stats_interval). Absent: OpenSync's default, 60 s.

survey.description: Also a raw on-channel survey of the radio (channel utilization for AP metrics, spec 3.8).

topology_query_window.description: Given to every agent: a property of the controller (spec §2.5). Absent: the rule is off.

gtp_underlay.description: The site's own GTP underlay (spec 8.2), such as 169.254.1.0/24: given, the registry allocates each pod an underlay for its role as a GRE parent (spec 8.6), a 169.254.N.0/24 that never overlaps this one. Absent: none.

run_root.description: Each agent's run directory is run_root/<pod_id> (its status, on a RAM disk on a gateway). Absent: the agents write their status in their state directories.

agents.description: How the agents run (spec §4). systemd: an emosa-agent@POD unit each, enabled and started by the fleet. supervised: the C fleet's own children, for a system without systemd (a router's busybox init): the link helper, then the agent, with /etc/default/emosa and /etc/default/emosa-POD in their environment, started again 3 s after one ends, stopped when its pod is forgotten and when the fleet ends; each one's output in LOG_ROOT/POD/agent.log (the run root, else the state root), kept to two files of 256 KiB. Absent: EMOSA_AGENTS from the fleet's environment or /etc/default/emosa, else systemd.

pods.description: Per-pod overrides of the agent settings above, by serial number.

vif.description: Ignored; the fronthaul VIF comes from the profile.
